set.layering_notes: Santa Cruz County housing programs sit in the Community Development and Infrastructure Department (CDI) Planning Division, Housing Section (HousingProgramsInfo@santacruzcountyCA.gov, (831) 454-2332), which runs the Measure J inclusionary program, the Affordable Housing Impact Fee, LMIHAF, PLHA and the County housing NOFA; the Human Services Department's Housing for Health Division (H4H, the CoC CA-508 lead) runs HHAP, Homekey and homeless programs; Behavioral Health holds BHSA; and the Housing Authority of the County of Santa Cruz (HACSC) supplies vouchers. The County is a non-entitlement jurisdiction for CDBG and HOME. County programs apply only to the unincorporated area (about half the population); Santa Cruz, Watsonville, Capitola and Scotts Valley run their own programs (Pass 3). cdi.santacruzcountyca.gov, santacruzcountyca.gov PDFs, santacruzhealth.org and housingforhealthpartnership.org open normally; the Board's IQM2 portal (santacruzcountyca.iqm2.com) renders by script and could not be listed, so Board items were taken from NOFA appendices and press coverage. Santa Cruz will not use BHSA for capital; its value to a developer is a 15 to 20 year project-based rental or operating subsidy on PSH units, which can replace or supplement PBVs while HACSC's RFP is paused. Source is the revised June 2026 Integrated Plan PDF on santacruzhealth.org. Audit reclassification: funding_type set to grant because the plan funds rental subsidies ($6,539,529), bundled rental and operating subsidies for permanent settings ($914,623) and bundled interim housing subsidies ($781,451) a year; the plan answers No to BHSA capital development, and 0% of subsidies are administered through flex pools in the budget tables.

reason: Plan PDF confirms Housing Interventions amounts and that BHSA funds housing rental and operating subsidies with no capital, so funding_type is grant.

set.typical_award_size: Monterey Bay Housing Trust is a revolving loan fund financed by the Monterey Bay Economic Partnership and Housing Trust Silicon Valley (created July 2016, initial $10 million goal exceeded; Dignity Health also listed as a financing partner). Recent Santa Cruz County loans: 2727 Mattison Lane, unincorporated county (MidPen Housing, 250 units for families and seniors at 30% to 80% AMI), $9,945,000 acquisition loan through the TECH Fund (April 23, 2025); Beverly Gardens, Scotts Valley (CRP Affordable Housing, 25 units with HACSC PBVs), $3,277,500 acquisition loan through the TECH Fund and Golden State Acquisition Fund (May 28, 2025); 4575 Scotts Valley Apartments (CRP, 100 units at 30% to 70% AMI), $2,000,000 predevelopment loan through the TECH Fund (May 30, 2025). Housing Trust reports 14 loans totaling $33 million in the Monterey Bay region.
set.per_unit_cap: Not published; recent Santa Cruz County loans ranged from $2,000,000 to $9,945,000 per project.
set.affordability_requirement: Affordable housing for low-income individuals and families, including special needs populations; recent loans served 30% to 80% AMI.
set.cycle_notes: No application round; every loan starts with a conversation with the Housing Trust lending team (Nick Friend, 408-703-3837 ext. 223; Stephaney Kipple, ext. 244).
set.audit_note: The MBHT program page lists Monterey Bay Economic Partnership and Dignity Health as financing partners; the County of Santa Cruz is not listed, so a County capital contribution remains unconfirmed. The Habitat 11 Harper Street 2020 loan was not re-checked.

reason: HTSV pages confirm the loans and rolling access; 4575 Scotts Valley was a $2,000,000 predevelopment loan and the MBHT page is a better program source.

set.typical_award_size: Standard state welfare exemption from property tax for low-income housing owned by a nonprofit or a limited partnership with a nonprofit managing general partner. The Assessor requires a Welfare Exemption claim with the BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate (BOE-277), the Supplemental Clearance Certificate for low-income housing (BOE-277-L1) and financial statements; BOE decides organizational eligibility and the Assessor decides whether the property use qualifies. A first filing is required for each new location and each year until granted, then annual filings.
set.affordability_requirement: Qualifies if financed with tax-exempt bonds or federal, state or local loans or grants with rents held to regulatory agreement limits, or if the owner receives low-income housing tax credits, or (nonprofit-owned) at least 90% of tenants are low-income households; exemption applies only to qualifying low-income units (80% AMI under state law).
set.next_deadline: File Welfare Exemption claims with the Assessor by February 15, 2027 for the 2027-28 roll; late claims carry a 10% penalty through December 31 and 15% after, capped at $250 in tax per organization per year.
set.cycle_notes: Annual filing due February 15; the Assessor mails renewal claims in late December to entities granted an exemption in the prior year.

reason: Old URL redirects to the new Assessor site; the Institutional Exemptions page confirms the low-income housing welfare exemption, required BOE-277 and BOE-277-L1 and the February 15 deadline.

set.typical_award_size: Chapter 24.16 Part 4 is now Fee Deferrals for Affordable Units (Sections 24.16.300 Units Eligible for Fee Deferrals and 24.16.310 Procedure for Deferral of Fees). Resolution NS-30,634 (adopted March 10, 2026) lets staff defer development review fees for 100 percent affordable housing projects: Building, Fire, Community Development, Parks, Police, Public Works, Water and similar fees may be deferred up to five years, or until certificate of occupancy if a substantially complete building permit application is filed, then up to about five more years on a payment plan with interest set annually by the Finance Director. Third-party review cost fees are collected in full; impact fees (Gov. Code 66007, SB 937), the Parks and Recreation Facilities Tax and the Quimby Fee cannot be deferred past certificate of occupancy; the Traffic Impact Fee is deferred under separate procedures. Fee waivers are not granted by staff and must still be requested from City Council; Resolution NS-30,635 waivers apply only to projects on City-owned land or buildings. Part 3 density bonus text and the childcare impact fee reduction for 100% affordable projects were not read (codepublishing.com 403).
set.per_unit_cap: None; deferral covers the eligible development review fees in full, subject to exclusions.
set.affordability_requirement: 100 percent affordable housing developments for the staff deferral policy; a 2019 City form indicated only very low and low income units were eligible for Part 4 fee relief (not re-confirmed).
set.next_deadline: Rolling. Submit the supplemental fee deferral application with the 100 percent affordable planning application (or with building plan check if no planning fees apply), then sign a fee deferral agreement and payment plan.
set.cycle_notes: Policy adopted March 10, 2026 (Resolution NS-30,634, Planning Commission recommendation February 5, 2026); eligibility determined by the Community Development Director, payment plan approved by the Finance Director.
set.audit_note: Prevailing wage left unclear: the deferral policy and city page are silent, and the Labor Code 1720 text on leginfo returned 403 so no stated rule was read; code text for Part 3 and the childcare fee reduction still needs confirmation.

reason: City page and Resolution NS-30,634 show Part 4 is now a staff fee deferral for 100 percent affordable projects, but no stated prevailing wage rule or Part 3 code text could be read.

set.typical_award_size: The 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan states that inclusionary in-lieu fees under Chapter 14-46 go to the City's Affordable Housing fund and are used for development, acquisition, rehabilitation and preservation of affordable units, and that PLHA, HOME, CDBG, CalHome and in-lieu fees provide gap financing for the First-Time Homebuyer and Housing Rehabilitation programs. The City has no active state HOME grant (last award $1,546,000 in 2011) and holds over $1,850,000 of HOME program income available for future HOME-eligible activities; it has made over 500 FTHB loans and has 280 inclusionary ownership units. The 2025-2029 plan does not mention Successor Agency property and states the City does not anticipate using publicly owned land for CDBG goals. No in-lieu fund balance, multifamily loan terms or application procedure is published.
set.audit_note: Consolidated Plan supports the fund's existence, HOME program income figure and 70% AMI inclusionary basis, but not multifamily award size, loan terms or the Successor Agency site claim; the documented uses of these funds are mainly homebuyer and owner rehab.

reason: The Consolidated Plan confirms the fund and HOME program income but publishes no multifamily award terms, cycle or fund balance, and does not support the Successor Agency property claim.

set.layering_notes: Capitola's fund is too small (about $144,000) to serve as gap financing; its value is as a local match or fee offset in a TCAC or HCD application, with capital from the County's Chapter 17.10 AHIF fund being unavailable inside city limits. The $25 per square foot impact fee is a significant cost on market-rate rental projects (the County charges $2 per habitable square foot on rentals), so mixed-income sponsors should model it; the fee feasibility analysis (EPS, 2021) warned rental development was marginal even before the increase. Density increases are available under the mixed-use AHO successor provisions for 20% lower income units (record below). Sources opened: 2023-2031 Housing Element PDF (DocumentCenter 1797), 2021 fee feasibility analysis (DocumentCenter 699) and the March 23, 2026 Annual Progress Report memo. Audit reclassification: funding_type set to loan because Housing Element Program 2.7 states the City uses the Housing Trust Fund to provide loans and grants (Housing Rehabilitation Loan and Grant Program, feasibility studies, and permanent financing of acquisition-rehab and new construction affordable projects); the balance is only about $144,000. The Housing Element also states a $6 per square foot impact fee for multifamily rental housing alongside the $25 per square foot fee, so confirm the rental rate with the City.

reason: Housing Element Program 2.7 states the trust fund provides loans and grants including permanent financing for affordable projects, so funding_type is loan.
